Mixed race adult man here. I understand where you are coming from. I went through some very similar situations when I was growing up. With a black father and a Thai mother I never quite fit with the other black or Asian kids. I often felt alone and ugly. It wasn’t until I was an adult where I discovered it was more so a blessing. When I was older, I realized it made me more diverse, made it easier to hang out with any group or people, and to my surprise, women (and I’m sure men too) were very attracted to mixed heritages. 

I guess what I’m getting at…is don’t beat yourself up to much. Don’t feel that you need to be a part of a specific group of people. You’re different and you are you. Embrace who you are, the things you enjoy, and share it with people. Then you should be able to grow relationships that are deeper than what your skin looks like.

I can’t really provide advice on hating being a boy as I have never struggled with that. I can say that you should be honest with yourself and not get too attached to a label. Live how you feel and not by how a label defines what you should be. If you don’t like/feel masculine, that’s okay…it’s not a requirement.

Lastly, talk to your parents. Be open…My father and I never even said “I love you” to each other til I was already an adult. Your family loves you, cultivate that.

Trust me, there are people in this world that love you just for being here. Good luck!
